type.notes: Flat positive 0.01em at every size (display included) rather than a negative ramp — Inter's optical sizing does the tightening. Display headings correct the left side-bearing with margin-left: -0.0618em. Sizes step per-breakpoint as percentages (223.5% → 394.1%); no clamp(), no fluid type.

notes: Ground truth is raw/olsonkundig.css + the rendered DOM; the frequency profile was used only to rank. Normalized away: Plyr's vendor custom properties (--plyr-*), the site's --vh/--winHeight JS fallback for --fillLVH/--fillSVH, and ~28 breakpoints (480–2560 min-width plus orientation and min-height queries) that exist because the layout is height-driven, not width-driven. 'statement-blur-dissolve' is recorded as property:'clip' because the schema has no 'filter' value — the real declaration is `transition: filter .8s linear` → `filter: blur(3rem)`. color.dark is OMITTED deliberately: craft.theme.supportsDark reports true, but the 'dark' palette it returns is identical to the light one — the site is permanently dark and never re-themes (meta.color_scheme: 'normal'). The probe's `respectsReducedMotion: false` / `prmRules: 0` is a FALSE NEGATIVE: there is no @media (prefers-reduced-motion) block, but the preference is read in JS, applied via `body.reduced-motion` rules, and surfaced to the user as a `role=switch` toggle plus an 'Enable Motion' notice — so the user-facing outcome is respected. Shadow list is effectively empty: the only box-shadows in the build are the gold rings of the `motion-pulse` animation on the active toggle. Tracking is uniform (0.17px @ 17px = 0.01em) at every size, which is the opposite of the corpus's usual size-scaled negative ramp — do not generalize it off a variable font.
